diagnosis: PolyNorm forms powers and squared powers in the input dtype before reduction. This permits fp16 overflow and premature rounding; an infinite mean square suppresses the corresponding normalized term. The observed fp16 case poly-02 has 23,541/32,768 mismatches, maximum absolute error 6.92785184, and unchanged inputs. The same-width fp32 control poly-03 passes with zero mismatches and maximum absolute error 8.73e-7. Intermediate overflow is inferred from source and this dtype-dependent behavior; intermediate values were not observed. Widening before arithmetic repairs the precision loss. FP64 also accommodates sixth powers throughout the finite fp32/bf16 range, unlike a simple FP32 promotion. Output allocation and final storage retain the input shape and dtype, and inputs remain read-only. The backward cache retains its existing FP32 contract; backward numerical robustness is outside this repair. Compilation, held-out correctness, and performance could not be tested through the supplied API; FP64 throughput and device support remain limitations.

edits.new:
# Widen before forming powers: even finite fp32 inputs can overflow
    # fp32 when raised to the sixth power for the cubic RMS reduction.
    # FP64 covers these intermediates for fp16, bf16, and fp32 inputs.
    X_row = tl.load(X_ptr + col_offsets, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float64)

    # Keep the weighted sum wide until the final output store.
    w0 = tl.load(W_ptr + 0).to(tl.float64)
    w1 = tl.load(W_ptr + 1).to(tl.float64)
    w2 = tl.load(W_ptr + 2).to(tl.float64)
    b = tl.load(B_ptr).to(tl.float64)
